items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: That's Alphonse Pico and John Cashman. There's the only two E flat players that I know of.

ctx.x: How many E flat clarinets are there in town now?

Two to my knowings. Who is that? That's Alphonse Pico and John Cashman. There's the only two E flat players that I know of. There may be some more in the union, these youngsters coming along, you know. But I noticed these school bands, I don't see any E flats. I see a lot of B flats. You see twenty or thirty B flats but you don't see no E. The fellas, I don't know, they're afraid of that instrument like they are the oboe. I hear those fellas, those oboe players, they say that the oboe jar is your head. I don't…
It's different. Yeah it's different. Did they have many oboe players when you were young?
